BUY-SIDE DUE DILIGENCE MEMORANDUM: CASCADE ENVIRONMENTAL SOLUTIONS, INC. (CES) CIM ANALYSIS
To: Marcus Yuen, Diane Holbrook (Thornfield Capital Partners, Fund III). Prepared for the deal team ahead of the July 14, 2025 IOI deadline.

1. BOTTOM LINE
Proceed to an IOI only on a re-based valuation and with conditions. The CIM's $17.1M Adjusted EBITDA (19.6%) is overstated by an arithmetic error, a likely double-count, and aggressive add-backs. Our base case is about $15.5M (downside about $14.1M). The CIM, the Customer/Backlog Report and the Excel exhibits, all prepared by Greenleaf, contradict one another on customers, balance sheet, income statement and capex. The largest customer (21.4% of revenue) has an MSA that expired March 31, 2025, with no renewal disclosed. A threshold mandate point: Thornfield's own memo says Fund III targets $30M-$100M EV and then says CES "fits squarely", but the seller's implied EV is $136.8M-$171.0M. Confirm Fund III concentration limits and co-invest before submitting.

2. ADJUSTED EBITDA (CIM VI.C; Excel "EBITDA Bridge"; App. B)
(a) Footing error. 12.1 + 1.9 + 0.8 + 1.2 + 0.4 + 0.3 + 0.1 = 16.8, not 17.1. The stated "total adjustments" of 4.7 is right; the 17.1 total is wrong. Corrected margin 19.2%; FY21-24 Adjusted EBITDA CAGR 20.1% (not 20.8%). EV effect at 8-10x: $2.4-3.0M.
(b) DEQ add-back ($1.2M = $875K settlement + $325K fees). Three problems. First, the Excel income statement books FY24 "Other Income/(Expense)" of $(875)K below EBIT. If the settlement sits below EBITDA, adding it back to reported EBITDA double-counts it (up to $0.875M). Second, Appendix B shows a $0.2M "legal/regulatory" add-back in FY23, so this is not isolated. Third, Thornfield's benchmark is a $200-500K annual regulatory run-rate, so only the excess is defensible: about $0.7-0.9M if the cost is in EBITDA, and about $0-0.1M if the settlement is below EBITDA. The CIM calls the matter both a "settlement agreement" and a "consent agreement"; obtain the instrument, 10-year enforcement history and ongoing obligations. obtain the instrument. The violation was improper storage of contaminated soil at the Portland yard, which Mr. Oakes owns (see 4). Oregon hazardous-waste penalties can reach $25,000 per day per violation (ORS 466.990, verified via search; confirm current text),.
(c) Related-party lease ($0.8M). The CIM's own Industry Overview (IV.C) says specialized environmental staging properties of comparable acreage lease for $1.0-1.2M annually, which contradicts the $600K "market" used for the add-back. A defensible add-back is $0.2-0.4M. The lease also runs to 2029 at $1.4M and the Excel projections keep $1.4M expense in FY25-27E, so the saving is not realizable unless the lease is amended or the property is acquired at closing.
(d) Owner compensation ($1.9M). The $2.4M includes unquantified "personal expenses" (tax and expense-allocation diligence needed). A $500K replacement for the CEO of an 412-employee, $87M-revenue business is thin. Each additional $250K costs about $2.0-2.5M of EV. Prior-year add-backs ($1.4/1.5/1.7M) do not equal Excel owner compensation ($2.1/2.2/2.3M) less $500K ($1.6/1.7/1.8M), so the method changed. The Excel projections also show owner compensation at zero in FY25-27E with no replacement CEO cost, which overstates projected EBIT.
(e) "Non-recurring" items. The relocation add-back has grown $0.1M, $0.2M, $0.4M (FY22-24), which looks recurring. The CIM says the Boise depot was established at 1880 Vista Avenue in 2018 yet the bridge describes a "relocation" to that address; reconcile it with the $0.5M FY24 depot capex line.
(f) Phantom units ($0.3M). Acceptable as non-cash, but see 5.
Illustrative bridge ($M): management 17.1; arithmetic -0.3; lease -0.5; DEQ -0.3 (Thornfield method); CEO cost -0.25; relocation -0.2 = about 15.5 (EV $124-155M at 8-10x). Downside (settlement below EBITDA, lease $1.2M, CEO $1.0M, relocation fully disallowed) = about 14.1 (EV $113-141M). These are our assumptions, subject to QoE. The 8.0-10.0x "comparables" are unsourced in the CIM and in our memo; request named transactions.

3. FINANCIAL STATEMENTS DO NOT RECONCILE (CIM App. A vs. Excel; FY24 unless noted)
- Gross profit $29.5M (33.8%) vs. $28.8M (33.0%); net income $5.0M vs. $6.7M.
- Excel EBIT is $11.1M with D&A of $4.2M shown beneath it, yet pre-tax income is computed without deducting D&A. Reported EBITDA ($12.1M) does not equal EBIT plus D&A ($15.3M) or EBIT ($11.1M). Excel EBIT also exceeds EBITDA less D&A by $1.5-3.2M in every year.
- Cash $2.3M vs. $4.1M; total assets $46.1M vs. $50.0M; PP&E $18.7M vs. $21.3M; equity $17.1M vs. $18.8M; total liabilities $29.0M vs. $31.2M.
- Debt. CIM: $17.3M ($14.2M term loan including $2.3M current, plus $3.1M revolver). Excel: current portion $1.8M plus term loan $14.2M plus revolver $3.1M = $19.1M. Net working capital is $11.8M in both but built from different lines. Net of cash and debt, the peg is about $11.8M (CIM) vs. $9.5M (Excel), a $2.3M swing in a cash-free/debt-free deal. The term loan matures Aug. 31, 2026.
-
Action: require audited FY22-24 statements and reconcile every line; the Excel exhibits say reported EBITDA is "per audited financials", yet it does not foot.

4. CUSTOMERS, BACKLOG AND CONTRACTS
- PNR ($18.7M, 21.4%). The MSA expired March 31, 2025, before both June 2025 documents. MSAs carry no minimum volume. Obtain the renewal or holdover terms, pricing, change-of-control and termination clauses, and refinery turnaround schedule. Making PNR renewal (or extension on acceptable terms) a signing condition is warranted. All customer contact must go through Greenleaf (no-contact rule); keep to that.
- Contract tenure. On the CIM's list, PNR, ODOT (annual, July renewal), Meridian (Dec. 2025), Willamette Steel (month-to-month) and City of Portland BES (annual) are $41.7M (47.8% of revenue) expiring, rolling or terminable in 2025. Adding Cascade Terminals, Puget Sound and Northern Pacific Rail takes it to $52.0M (59.6%) by end-2026; only Columbia Basin Power ($7.3M, Dec. 2027) and Tidewater (Mar. 2027) run longer. "Significant majority under multi-year MSAs" and "10-year relationships" are overstated; by the Report's start dates average top-10 tenure is about 7.9 years, not 8+.
- The CIM and the Report name different customers at ranks 6-10 (CIM: Cascade Terminals, Puget Sound Utilities, City of Portland BES, Northern Pacific Rail, Tidewater; Report: Clearwater Municipal Utility District, Northshore Industrial Park, Summit Materials, Timberline Construction, Harborview Port Authority) with identical revenues and similar expirations. Start dates also differ (PNR 2011 vs. 2012; ODOT 2013 vs. 2014; Meridian 2014 vs. 2017; Columbia Basin 2017 vs. 2016). The customer list is therefore unverified; demand a customer-by-customer revenue file tied to the ledger.
- Government revenue. The Report says government contracts are about 5% of revenue, "primarily ODOT", but ODOT alone is 10.4%.
- Geography. CIM: about 75% Oregon/Washington; Report: 82.3%. The Report mentions a Sacramento "satellite operation" that the CIM's facility list omits.
- Backlog ($42.6M) is defined to include work where terms are "reasonably estimable", which includes MSA task orders without commitment. It is about six months of revenue. $33.0M converts in 2025, against $98.5M of FY25E revenue; expected pipeline yield is $11.0-12.6M (35-40% win rate), so $74.0M "visibility" is unweighted. The 2025 forecast needs about $53M from book-and-burn work. H1 2025 actuals should already exist; request YTD results (the CIM is Dec. 2024 data). Also request backlog by contract, funded vs. unfunded, with PFAS broken out.

5. PFAS AND PROJECTIONS
- Management projects PFAS of $14.0M in FY25E (+126%) and $22.0M in FY26E, which is 64% of FY24-26 incremental revenue ($15.8M of $24.7M). Excel shows traditional remediation about flat in FY25E (+1.2%), so PFAS carries essentially all remediation growth. Thornfield's benchmark of 30-50% growth implies $8.1-9.3M in FY25 and $10.5-14.0M in FY26. That benchmark rests on one GreenWorks data point and the Thornfield memo's own market-growth estimate (25-35%), so treat it as a judgment, not a measurement.
- Capacity. The company has two PEs after a January 2025 retirement, and PE sign-off is required for site assessments, work plans and closure reports. Test a PE hiring plan (6-12 month recruiting) and any practice-of-engineering licensing exposure.
- Capex mismatch. PFAS capex falls to $0.3M in FY25E while PFAS revenue more than doubles.
- Regulatory (verified; as of memo date and current). EPA finalized six-PFAS drinking water standards in April 2024. On May 14, 2025 EPA announced it would keep the PFOA/PFOS 4 ppt limits, extend compliance from 2029 to 2031, and rescind the PFHxS, PFNA, HFPO-DA and hazard-index limits. The D.C. Circuit on Jan. 21, 2026 denied EPA's motion to vacate the hazard-index portions in AWWA v. EPA, No. 24-1188, so the rule's final form remains unsettled. EPA said on Sept. 17, 2025 it will retain the CERCLA hazardous-substance designation of PFOA/PFOS. The CIM's description of "regulatory tailwinds" therefore needs a delayed-demand sensitivity, and the demand is driven by water systems and CERCLA sites more than by CES's industrial base.
- Liability. Handling PFAS creates CERCLA arranger/transporter and disposal-chain exposure; check PFAS exclusions in pollution and professional liability policies.
- Projected margins (19.6% to 21.5%) rely on mix shift to PFAS that is unproven; the Excel projections also omit CEO cost (see 2(d)).

6. CAPEX, FLEET AND WORKING CAPITAL
- Maintenance capex is $3.0M (3.4% of revenue) vs. a Thornfield benchmark of 5-7% ($4.4-6.1M). Correction to our memo: the midpoint is 6% = $5.2M, not $5.5M. Counterpoints: the fleet averages 4.5 years and $22M replacement value, and the CIM says maintenance is flat at $3.0M while Excel shows $2.4-3.0M rising. Obtain the fleet register, age and condition survey and a deferral analysis. A $1-2.5M reduction to cash flow is plausible.
- DSO. Stated 52 days. Computed from year-end AR $16.9M and revenue $87.3M = 70.7 days (82 days with unbilled revenue $2.7M); about 68-71 days every year FY21-24. A 52-day DSO implies AR of $12.4M, so $4.5M of AR is unexplained. Age the receivables and test collectibility, disputes and unbilled revenue recognition.

7. LEGAL AND STRUCTURAL DILIGENCE
- Stock purchase assumes all historical liabilities. Require a Phase I/II on the Portland yard, an environmental indemnity from Mr. Oakes (as landlord and seller), escrow or holdback, and a special indemnity for the DEQ matter. R&W insurance will likely exclude known environmental matters and PFAS. Make the property purchase or a new market lease with a long term and environmental allocation a closing deliverable (the process letter asks bidders to address this).
- Permits. Confirm "DEQ Contractor License ENV-2009-04821". Oregon DEQ's contractor licensing is for UST services (OAR ch. 340, div. 160), and its scope should be verified. Confirm the four-state hazardous-waste transporter permits, EPA ID, and any change-of-control notice or reissuance requirements.
- Contracts. Review change-of-control, assignment and termination-for-convenience clauses (ODOT, City of Portland, utilities).
- Equity and phantom units. The 32% minority holders and any shareholder agreement determine drag-along mechanics. The phantom plan is cash-settled at closing; amount, holders and tax cost are undisclosed and not visible on the balance sheet. Treat it as a debt-like/transaction expense. It also removes the retention hook; replace it with new equity or rollover incentives. Consider IRC section 280G (private-company shareholder-approval exception) for change-in-control payments.
- Key people. Mr. Oakes (age 61, 68% owner) leaves within 18-24 months with no named CEO successor. Ms. Prewitt (remediation, key client relationships) is described as joining in 2007, before the 2009 founding; clarify predecessor entities. Require retention agreements as signing conditions (GreenWorks lesson), a sale-of-business non-compete for Mr. Oakes, and employment confirmations for Prewitt, Cahill and the PEs.
- HSR. At EV above $126.4M (2025 threshold, effective Feb. 21, 2025; confirm the current figure and new form requirements), a premerger filing is likely required; build 30 days (plus any second request risk) into the Q4 2025 timetable. Check state premerger notification statutes.

8. IOI RECOMMENDATIONS
Bid on a trailing basis using $14.1-15.5M diligence-adjusted EBITDA, not 17.1M, with price protection: (1) EV range framed as a multiple of QoE-confirmed EBITDA; (2) price/earn-out linkage to PFAS delivery; (3) conditions: PNR extension, lease/real-estate resolution, retention agreements, DEQ closure letter; (4) NWC peg set at closing on a reconciled basis; (5) debt-like items including phantom units, DEQ obligations, accrued legal and capex catch-up. Send Greenleaf a written question list now: PNR status, customer reconciliation, audited statements, regulatory history, backlog schedule, YTD 2025 results, PFAS pipeline, PE plan, fleet survey.
